intent: v1 of this plan was substantially wrong and is withdrawn: it reported three divergences of which only ONE is real. Two were manufactured by comparing a peak against a mean, and a 10,000 rpm corner against a 19,500 rpm solve. This v2 addresses the single real like-for-like divergence — continuous shaft torque at 19,500 rpm, 119.7 analytic vs 81.558 measured — and asks whether the deliverable should prefer either number at all.
why_now: The comparison defect is already fixed at source (basis and operating_point are load-bearing; mismatches report as incomparable; four proveCatch cases). What remains is a decision about what the workbook should print when a requirement and a capability disagree.
explicitly_not_doing: not deleting or altering 145.7 or 334 — both correct for what they describe
not rewriting contract quantities in place
not re-opening the EM or architecture findings
success_criteria: one declared load case drives every comparison
governance decided at a single provenance-aware point
gate fires only on unresolved like-for-like divergence
the workbook makes the chosen basis visible
